Drafts for today: (1) why a Philly seller says yes to terms, (2) a 'best seller-finance deal you've seen' reply magnet, (3) a 25-years-in origin story.

drafts.draft_en:
Why would a Philly seller take payments instead of cash?

1/ Monthly income they don't have to manage
2/ A better price than a cash buyer offers
3/ Taxes spread out instead of one big hit
4/ A paid-off house that just sits there earns them nothing

If you never ask, the answer is always no.
drafts.pattern: numbered 'why would a seller accept seller financing' explainer (brianbeers format) + 'ask the seller' close
drafts.video_tip: Talking head, 30-40s, hold up four fingers and count the reasons. Keep point 3 general (no tax advice); tell sellers to talk to their CPA.

drafts.draft_en:
What's the best seller-finance deal you've ever seen?

Price, rate, down payment, term.

I'll go first in the replies.
drafts.pattern: one-line question reply magnet + 'I'll go first' commitment
drafts.video_tip: Skip video. Post it, then reply within a minute with one real deal you've done or seen (numbers only, no addresses or seller names). Answer every reply in the first hour.

drafts.draft_en:
25 years ago I didn't know what a deed was.

Today I find deals other investors never see.

No degree. No rich uncle.

Just one ugly first property and the habit of asking sellers better questions.

What was your first deal?
